output.title: Model deprecation is a workflow risk, not just a tech detail
output.body:
If you run a small business and use AI in a workflow, model deprecation hides in the rebuild cost. A model version changes, a feature disappears, or the route you relied on no longer behaves the same. The work did not vanish. It moved back onto your desk.

That is the real decision: do you build around a tool and model setup that can be changed under you, or do you keep the process simple enough that a change is easy to absorb? For an owner, that is not an abstract AI question. It is a control question.

Bareni’s diagnostic starts with the recurring workflow and whether AI honestly fits it. In that conversation, the useful check is plain: if the model behind this automation were unavailable in 12 months, what would rebuilding take compared with the time you gain now?

If the answer is “not much,” the risk may be fine. If the answer is “I would have to untangle half the process,” the automation is carrying hidden complexity. No tool removes that risk entirely; Zapier, Make, and n8n can help structure the workflow, but they do not make deprecation disappear.

The practical next step is to write down that fallback cost before you approve anything. Human approval still belongs at the end.
